title: AI underwriting for lenders and insurers: what to automate first
description: Where AI pays in underwriting: the reading, not the decision. 19 tools checked, the US and EU rules, our benchmark data and three builds.
summary: AI underwriting reads the application and its documents, pulls out the facts an underwriter needs, and helps score the risk. The reading is where the hours go and where AI is now reliable. The decision is where the rules bite, so it stays explainable and a person stays accountable.
verdict: Point AI at the reading, not the decision. Underwriters spend about 39% of their time on admin and other non-core work, and current models read long financial documents with zero mistakes in our sealed benchmark when two models check each other. Keep the risk decision with an explainable model and a named underwriter: US lenders and New York insurers must give specific reasons for a decline, and 30 US jurisdictions now expect insurers to govern and test their AI.

pickElse: Consumer lending where the score is the product: start with the AI credit scoring guide. The decline reasons are the regulated part.
Life and health insurer: start from a rules engine such as Swiss Re Magnum or Munich Re ALLFINANZ. AI earns its keep summarising medical evidence, not making the call.
Commercial P&C carrier or MGA buried in broker submissions: an intake product (Cytora, Convr, FurtherAI, Sixfold) may beat a build. Benchmark it on 50 of your own submissions first.
The question is price, not whether to take the risk: look at actuarial pricing platforms such as Akur8, Earnix or hyperexponential.

rules.name: Regulation B, 12 CFR 1002.9
rules.what: US lenders must give the specific main reasons for a decline within 30 days, whatever model made it.

rules.name: NYDFS Circular Letter No. 7
rules.what: New York insurers must test AI and outside data for unfair discrimination, keep board oversight, stay responsible for vendor tools and give specific reasons and data sources for adverse decisions.

rules.name: NAIC Model Bulletin on AI
rules.what: Insurers need a written AI program with governance, risk controls and vendor oversight. California, Colorado and New York have their own rules instead.

rules.name: Colorado SB21-169
rules.status: Life; auto and health from 15 Oct 2025
rules.what: Insurers must test outside data and models for unfair discrimination, fix harm found and report to the Division.

rules.name: EU AI Act, Annex III
rules.what: Credit scoring of people and life and health insurance risk pricing are high-risk uses. Plan logging, human oversight and documentation now if you operate in the EU.

howToTest: Take 50 past files with known outcomes, including your messiest scans and longest packets.
Have your underwriters write the right value for every fact before any AI reads the files, and lock that answer key.
Run each tool on the same files. Count wrong facts apart from blanks, and require a page and quote for every fact.
For scoring, compare an explainable model with your current method on the same past files, and check that the decline reasons make sense to an underwriter.
Measure cost and time per file, and how many files still need a person.

buyVsBuild.buy: Buy when your line is standard, the vendor already handles your submission formats, and you are happy to run inside its workbench.
buyVsBuild.build: Build when your own loss history and appetite are your edge, or when you need the reading step to feed systems you already own. The reading layer is small and swappable; the decision logic is yours.

watchOuts: You stay responsible for a vendor's model. New York requires audit rights in the contract.
Models trained on past approvals repeat past bias. Test approval gaps across applicant groups before launch and on a schedule after.
A model's confidence score is not a warning sign. In our benchmark, wrong answers came back rated 70 to 100.
Vendor claims such as faster quotes are measured on the vendor's chosen customers. Ask for a benchmark on your own files.
